summary: 8 changes ordered by UNBLOCKED VALUE rather than by the dependency chain, because two changes deliver real value with no dependency on UAR at all. Wave 1 (parallel, start now): C-002 [UPSTREAM, the long pole], C-001 (one line; removes the surrealdb lockstep pin and UAR's whole transitive tree from the DEFAULT build), C-003 (the actual bug fix: resolve_sidecar_command is hardcoded to the Telegram stem so UAR falls through to a bare PATH lookup; also replaces the opaque `os error 2` with an error naming every path searched), C-005 (config). Wave 2: C-004 (ship the binary), C-006 (supervisor). Wave 3: C-007 (HTTP/SSE driver), C-008 (console controls). Zero new third-party dependencies.
key_insight: C-006's fake contract-honouring `uar-sidecar` (prints READY:<port>, serves /healthz, exits on stdin EOF) means librefang's TESTS do not wait on the upstream C-002 blocker — only the real end-to-end verification does. That keeps C-006/C-007/C-008 implementable and reviewable while the upstream change is in flight.
first_change_to_apply: C-001 (smallest, unblocked, immediately valuable) or C-003 (the bug fix). Open C-002 upstream in parallel — it is the long pole and every day it is not started adds a day to the phase.
